title: Heuristic Evaluation
body:
**Heuristic evaluation** has a small group of evaluators inspect an interface against a list of
design principles, recording every violation. It needs no users, takes hours, and finds a large
fraction of the problems in a system.

The method: each evaluator goes through the interface alone, so nobody is influenced by anybody
else, notes every violation with the heuristic it breaks and a severity rating, and the
findings are combined afterwards. Three to five evaluators is the usual number, because one
finds roughly a third of the problems and the returns fall off sharply after five.

[[Nielsen's Heuristics]] is the standard list of ten used as the checklist.

```
found:      inconsistent terminology, missing feedback, unclear error messages,
            no undo, hidden system status
missed:     that the task itself is wrong for this user, that the vocabulary
            means something else in their profession, that the flow assumes
            information they do not have yet
```

The second row is the limitation, and it is structural. An expert inspecting an interface
evaluates it against principles, with no real goal in play, so anything depending on what a
particular user is trying to do stays invisible. That is what [[Usability Testing]] is
for, and the two methods are run together because each finds what the other misses.
